To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LTQDs can be used to fabricate high speed VCSELs emitting at 1225 and at 1250 nm.
the LTQDs grown at low temperature of ~ 400 degC are suitable for high speed and high power VCSELs.
LTQDs are a promising approach to achieve high-speed and high-temperature VCSELs in the wavelength range of 1.2-1.3 μm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, growth and fabrication of InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots grown by molecular beam epitaxy at low temperatures.
the development of high-speed 1.3 µm VCSELs based on InGaAs LTQDs.
the design, fabrication and performance analysis of high-speed VCSELs based on LTQDs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LTQD material is a suitable candidate for high speed VCSELS.
LTQD-VCSELs have reached the same performance levels as the best InP-based VCSELs.
LTQD-VCSELs are the best candidate for high speed and temperature stable long wavelength VCSELs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LTQD-VCSELs are able to reach a modulation bandwidth of more than 10 GHz at a wavelength of 1.25 µm.
we have shown the possibility to achieve high-speed modulation in 1.2 um wavelength VCSELs based on LTQDs.
LTQDs are a very promising material for high-speed VCSELs, which is also demonstrated by a 12 GHz 1.25 μm VCSEL, which was the fastest 1.25-μm VCSEL reported so far.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LTQD-VCSELs can reach modulation bandwidths of 10 GHz, while emitting in the 1.2 μm spectral window, which is of interest for optical interconnects and free space optical communication.
the high-speed modulation of VCSELs based on LTQDs is not limited by the carrier transport, but rather by the gain saturation and the differential gain.
